ladder.why: Builds between queries break static prefix sums, so you need a tree with O(log n) point update and range query.

ladder.teaches: a Fenwick tree for prefix sums
ladder.why: The Fenwick loop at its simplest: query the prefix of smaller ranks, then add 1 at your own rank.

ladder.teaches: a Fenwick tree for prefix sums
ladder.why: Moving a dividend is two point updates and a price is a prefix sum over days, in an OA story.
Values up to 2^31 cannot index an array, so you rank them first and then count with a Fenwick tree.
Fix the middle element, then multiply two compressed Fenwick counts (greater before, smaller after).
Each arrival is a +1 on a range and the answer is the global max, the canonical lazy segment tree over compressed endpoints.
Rewriting a weighted range query as a combination of two plain range sums, each kept in its own Fenwick tree under point updates.

ladder.teaches: a Fenwick tree for prefix sums
ladder.why: An OA string story that is an inversion count once each character is mapped to its target position.

ladder.teaches: a Fenwick tree for prefix sums
ladder.why: Run the inserts in reverse and use the Fenwick tree to find the k-th free slot by binary descent.
The fixed-middle idea with max instead of count: prefix-max Fenwick trees over compressed prices.
Sorting by price turns each price interval into an index range for a range-max query, with no updates (sparse table or segment tree).
Lazy range assignment with range-min queries over compressed half-open ranges.
An LIS whose transition is a max over a value window: a max segment tree over value ranks, point-raised as you scan.

notes: No plain 'Range Sum Query - Mutable' exists in the bank, so the first rung is the wall-building query (point update, range count). Lazy propagation has only onsite/phone-screen problems (Uber, Walmart); there is no OA lazy problem. Taken from outside the pools (in no other pool): tcs-count-smaller-prior-elements, tcs-count-array-inversions, amazon-longest-increasing-subsequence-bounded-difference (its bank statement is truncated before the rules; the repair restores them from the example and the solution).
